benchmarks.task_description:
Pin the Source Control list setting in the workspace contract

## Description

Commit 7a2099c added `scm.repositories.visible: 0` to `opentlv.code-workspace`, but `validate_workspace` requires empty shared settings, so `scripts/integration.py fast` fails and Main smoke is red on `main`.

The workspace contract now pins exactly this one editor-only setting. Any other shared setting, or a different value, is still rejected, so build settings continue to need their own integration contract.

## Related Issue

Refs OpenTLV/opentlv-testlab#2

## Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Maintenance
- [x] Tooling / CI
- [ ] Documentation

## Testing

Completed locally on Windows:

- `python -m pre_commit validate-config`: passed
- `python -B scripts/integration.py fast`: passed; it failed with the reported error before the fix
- `python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_integration.py`: 25 tests passed, 1 skipped
- `python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_quality.py`: 35 tests passed
- `python -B tests/test_bootstrap.py`: 18 tests passed
- `python -m pre_commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: passed

Pending on GitHub:

- Workspace PR checks on Linux, Windows and macOS
- Workspace Main on `main` after merge

## Checklist

- [x] Changes are focused on the workspace repository and the stated scope.
- [x] Relevant documentation is updated.
- [x] Notable changes are recorded in CHANGELOG.md using issue references when available.
- [x] Completed validation and any pending or unrun checks are described above.

CLAUDE.md: commit with your own identity, seedds' is his own

## What and why

Follows up #244. The wording there, "never upstream's", is still wrong for one case: @seedds also commits here, and for him the seedds identity is his own. The real rule is to commit as yourself.

The bullet now says the `git -c user.name=seedds` line at the end of AGENTS.md is seedds' own identity for his repository. Anyone else who copies it attributes their commits, and the `From:` line of patches from `scripts/patches.py export`, to him.

## Checked

- Tests: `python3 scripts/patches.py check` passes. Only `CLAUDE.md` changed.

## Scope

- [x] No vendored file (`dm/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `ref/`, `AGENTS.md`) is edited directly
- [x] No keys, game files or data extracted from a game in the change or the attachments

Fixes #637

on windows a deleted generation folder can hang around for a moment with its files already gone, and find reported damaged data instead of rebuilding. a generation folder with no generation.json and no files.jsonl now counts as missing, so it rebuilds like #618. one that still has its files but a bad manifest still reports damaged.

two new tests in test_state_recovery.py, the emptied-folder one fails without the fix.

benchmarks.task_description:
Map initial status in set_dpid_strategy_to_enum

## Summary

Follow-up to #685. The initial status is loaded from the cloud once at startup and stored as-is, while the local strategy only converts later MQTT updates. For Enum datapoints the cloud reports the same raw values as the device (e.g. `hot` in #318), so the initial value was rejected until the device pushed an update.

`set_dpid_strategy_to_enum` now also applies its mapping to the initial status when it matches a raw value of the quirk's mapping. Like the strategy, it only applies to devices with local support.

`map_dpid_initial_status_values` stays for cases where the cloud reports another shape (e.g. `"false"`/`"true"` for the Duux fan, whose quirk is unaffected). The docs example no longer needs it.

## Test plan

- New parametrized test in `tests/builder/test_device_quirk.py`: mapped value, unchanged value, no status, and non-local device.
- Existing Duux quirk tests still pass.
- `pytest`, ruff, ty, pylint and Prettier pass.

## Related issue

Related to #318

benchmarks.task_description:
Let the Choose dialog pick NSZ and XCZ files

## What and why

The per-row Choose... dialog only offered nsp and xci (nsp for DLC), so NSZ and XCZ files were greyed out. The folder scan (`classify`) and the build script already accept them, and the launcher installs nsz on demand when a selected path is compressed. That check looks at the selected paths, so it also covers files picked through this dialog.

Base and update now accept nsp, xci, nsz and xcz. DLC accepts nsp and nsz. The allowed types moved into a small helper, `BuildModel.allowedFileTypes(for:)`, with a unit test. The Qt front end has no filter and is unchanged.

Fixes #236

## Checked

- Tests: `cd frontend && swift test` passes (460 tests, 15 skipped). `python3 scripts/patches.py check` passes.
- Visual QA: not applicable, no layout change.
- Run on a device or Mac: not run, the app was not launched. The dialog filter is covered by the helper test only.

## Scope

- [x] No vendored file is edited directly
- [x] Not an engine or game profile change
- [x] No keys, game files or data extracted from a game
